 "content": "from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    def dominant_line(vals):
        counts = Counter(vals)
        color, n = counts.most_common(1)[0]
        return color, n / len(vals)

    # Grid dividers are long, nearly uniform rows and columns; sparse colored
    # corner markers may interrupt them.
    row_lines = [r for r in range(h)
                 if dominant_line(grid[r])[0] != bg and dominant_line(grid[r])[1] >= 0.75]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if (lambda d: d[0] != bg and d[1] >= 0.75)(dominant_line([grid[r][c] for r in range(h)]))]

    # A final divider on the extreme right is an outer margin in this encoding,
    # not an additional output-cell boundary.
    if col_lines and col_lines[-1] == w - 1 and len(col_lines) > 2:
        col_lines = col_lines[:-1]

    out = []
    for r0, r1 in zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:]):
        row = []
        for c0, c1 in zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:]):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1], grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            counts = Counter(v for v in corners if v != bg)
            # A marked color is carried into the reduced cell when its corner
            # pattern gives it a strict three-of-four majority. Otherwise retain
            # the original interior/background color.
            marked = [v for v, n in counts.items() if n >= 3]
            row.append(marked[0] if marked else bg)
        out.append(row)
    return out
"
}

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    def dominant(seq):
        color, n = Counter(seq).most_common(1)[0]
        return color, n / len(seq)

    row_info = [dominant(row) for row in grid]
    col_info = [dominant([grid[r][c] for r in range(h)]) for c in range(w)]
    # Uniform lattice strokes contrast with the repeated cell-interior color.
    rows = [r for r, (color, frac) in enumerate(row_info)
            if color != bg and frac >= 0.72]
    cols = [c for c, (color, frac) in enumerate(col_info)
            if color != bg and frac >= 0.72]
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return [[bg]]

    divider_colors = {row_info[r][0] for r in rows} | {col_info[c][0] for c in cols}
    out = []
    for r0, r1 in zip(rows, rows[1:]):
        row = []
        for c0, c1 in zip(cols, cols[1:]):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1], grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            # A matching non-divider color at all four lattice corners encodes
            # the reduced cell; otherwise it is the interior/background color.
            if corners.count(corners[0]) == 4 and corners[0] not in divider_colors:
                row.append(corners[0])
            else:
                row.append(bg)
        out.append(row)

    # The source can have unused lattice margins; crop to encoded cells.
    marked = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(out) for c, value in enumerate(row)
              if value != bg]
    if not marked:
        return [[bg]]
    r0 = min(r for r, _ in marked); r1 = max(r for r, _ in marked)
    c0 = min(c for _, c in marked); c1 = max(c for _, c in marked)
    return [row[c0:c1 + 1] for row in out[r0:r1 + 1]]
